answer: Delayed hardware-key registration: each new identity pays a nonrefundable 0.02 ETH relay fee and waits 48 hours before transacting, with the fee doubling on repeated machine fingerprints. At a wharf, a relay signs one identity per hardware key. A plume of duplicate attempts is throttled, and every clone pays the doubled fee. An island deployment test checks unique fingerprints, so cloning N identities costs N fees plus N×48 idle hours, keeping honesty cheaper.
